full_text:
Core Lightning node operators are being told to go offline while a two-week embargo holds.

Plus the first quantum-resistant Bitcoin transaction mined on mainnet, Coinbase's Bitcoin-backed mortgage goes nationwide, and Strategy adds $1.59B to its reserve ↓

Today, @marshallmixing and @katemparkman dig into:

• Critical vulnerabilities in Core Lightning: maintainers told every node operator to upgrade or restart with the --offline flag. Details under a two-week embargo — the bugs surfaced through AI-generated vulnerability reports that proved real. If you run a Lightning node, act now.

• The first quantum-resistant Bitcoin transaction was mined on mainnet: @StarkWareLtd submitted it through Marathon's Slipstream service and shared the news live at Bitcoin Asia. Non-standard transactions that work today at roughly $150 each.

• @coinbase's Bitcoin-backed mortgage is live nationwide: pledge 250% of the down payment in BTC, get a conforming Fannie Mae first mortgage plus a second loan against the coins. No margin calls just because the price drops.

• Pakistan released a full licensing framework for crypto exchanges, custody, lending, and derivatives: apply by September 5 or cease operations.

• Quick headlines: JPMorgan is considering its own stablecoin per the Wall Street Journal, HashKey Cloud joins Bitcoin staking on @Stacks, and @galaxyhq says last week's rise was Bitcoin's largest weekly dollar gain ever.

• Treasury tracker: @strive +1,110 BTC (21,356), @EMPD_BTC -100 (1,179). Pipeline: Alpha Modus signed a $254M PIPE for 3,170 BTC, Genius Group plans $827M over five years, @_ALCPB raising €21M. @strategy: no buys, no sells; +$1.59B USD reserve, $136M more STRC bought back.

• Follow us @goodforbtc for clips all week.
